Nevermind! I figured it out.

Here's what I did to get the order of the rows (I'm new to R, so forgive my clunky code):

tree <- read.newick("tree.iqtree.treefile")
thetree <- ggtree(tree)

distances <- as.data.frame(as.matrix(alignment_dist))

thetree_datasubset <- subset(thetree$data,thetree$data$isTip==TRUE)
thetree_datasubset_sorted <- thetree_datasubset[order(thetree_datasubset$y, decreasing = TRUE),]
sorted_labels <- thetree_datasubset_sorted[,1]
reordered_distances <- distances[sorted_labels]

gheatmap(thetree,reordered_distances, colnames = FALSE)

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am trying to overlay a maximum credibility clade over a sample of the trees in the posterior (produced by beast), e.g.:

trees = lapply(rep(50, 10), rcoal)  # Example sample of posterior trees.
class(trees) = 'multiPhylo'
tree = rcoal(50)                    # Maximum credibility tree.
p = ggtree(trees, layout='rectangular', color='skyblue', alpha=0.3)
p = p + geom_tree(data=tree) + theme_tree2()

However, when plotting this, all the roots line up, whereas in reality, it is the tips that should line up (because these are sampled at a specific point in time). I know I can use the mrsd setting in ggtree(), but then I cannot do the same with geom_tree(), which then plots the two in very different points of the axis, e.g.:

p = ggtree(trees, layout='rectangular', color='skyblue', alpha=0.3, mrsd=as.Date('2010-01-01'))
p = p + geom_tree(data=tree) + theme_tree2()

Does anyone know how I could get by this problem, or alternatively right align the trees being plotted?

messages.subject: Export tip labels defined in a clade
messages.subject_clean: Export tip labels defined in a clade
messages.body_plain:
I'm new to ggtree - it is an amazing tool, congrats.

Is it possible to export a list of tip labels (in my case these are sample names) that have been defined into clades on the tree based on branch node points? i.e. to export a list of all tip labels that are contained within a defined clade. e.g. as a list I can export as a .csv or .txt file, or just copy and paste out of R.

Here's an example of what I mean using a fake pairwise distance matrix:

# Generate dataframe with example pairwise distances
Samples <- c('Sample_A', 'Sample_B', 'Sample_C', 'Sample_D', 'Sample_E')
Sample_A <- c(0, 3.16, 1, 1.41, 3)
Sample_B <- c(3.16, 0, 3, 2.83, 1)
Sample_C <- c(1, 3, 0, 1, 2.83)
Sample_D <- c(1.41, 2.83, 1, 0, 2.65)
Sample_E <- c(3, 1, 2.83, 2.65, 0)
df = data.frame(Samples, Sample_A, Sample_B, Sample_C, Sample_D, Sample_E, header=TRUE,row.names=c(1))
df
# Turn dataframe into cluster to generate Newick tree
hclustfunc <- function(x) hclust(x, method="complete")
distfunc <- function(x) as.dist((1-cor(t(x)))/2)
d <- distfunc(df)
fit <- hclustfunc(d)
plot(fit)
# Produce Newick file
class(fit) # check that class is hclust
my_tree <- as.phylo(fit)
write.tree(phy=my_tree, file="ExampleTree.newick") # Writes a Newick file to disc
class(my_tree)
# Produce ggtree from Newick file
p <- ggtree(my_tree) + geom_tiplab(size=8) + ggplot2::xlim(0, 0.5)
p
# define clades
p2 <- p + geom_hilight(node=7, fill="#e31a1c", alpha=.4) +
  geom_hilight(node=9, fill="#0331E9", alpha=.4)
p2

That code produces a dendrogram with a couple of clades defined that looks like this:

What I would like is to get a list of samples that are contained within the clades, so for example the output of the node=7 clade would be c('Sample_E', 'Sample_B'); and the output for node=9 clade would be c('Sample_C', 'Sample_A'). I would then like to do downstream analyses on the different clades so I need them labelled, e.g. Clade 1 and Clade 2.

I know I can just read the sample names off manually in this example but my real data has >500 samples so I need an automated way of getting the sample names!

Thanks,
Will
